headlines.article_text: New York City man shot in car with child present by ICE agents: mayor Skip Navigation Markets Business Investing Tech Politics & Policy Video Watchlist Investing Club PRO Livestream Menu Members of law enforcement gather at the scene after a shooting reportedly involving US Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) officers in the Bronx borough of New York City, US, Oct. 8, 2026. David Dee Delgado | Reuters U.S. immigration agents shot and wounded a man on Thursday in his car with a child present in the Marble Hill neighborhood of New York City, according to the mayor, city police and eyewitnesses. Federal immigration agents have shot at least 21 people since Republican President Donald Trump returned to office, 7 fatally, sparking protests across the U.S. Critics contend ​that Trump's push to ramp up deportations has led to an increasing number of violent confrontations, and accuse the administration of resisting accountability for the agents involved. Trump has said many migrants must be deported, blaming them, often in sweeping terms, for financial fraud and violent crimes. "Early reports indicate agents surrounded (the man) and a 5-year-old child in his car before firing multiple rounds," New York Mayor Zohran Mamdani said in a statement. "I have been on the phone with President Trump and (Homeland Security) Secretary Mullin, negotiating the release of the man ICE agents shot. Those negotiations were unsuccessful," Mamdani said in a press conference late in the evening. He said he demanded from the Trump administration that ICE stop its enforcement actions in New York City. "These actions are making the city less safe," Mamdani said. "This city wants ICE out. We want ICE out of our city, ICE out of our schools, ICE out of our hospitals, ICE out of our streets, ICE away from our kids." The mayor said the child in the car is physically unharmed. New York Police Commissioner Jessica Tisch said NYPD has located the child with a family member after a wellness check. The Department of Homeland Security, ICE's parent agency, said in a statement ICE officers were conducting a "targeted enforcement operation" in the Bronx, New York, to arrest a man from the Dominican Republic with a prior criminal conviction. The man, identified as 28 years old, had been arrested twice in New York City in 2023 and 2025, according to NYPD Commissioner Tisch. "During the incident, an ICE officer discharged his weapon and the criminal illegal alien was injured," DHS said, adding that ICE officers rendered immediate aid. "The individual is alive and at a local hospital." The shooting occurred at around 4 p.m. ET (2000 GMT), DHS said. Working at a restaurant near the shooting, Pedro Almarez said he heard shots fired and went outside to see several officers wearing ICE attire at the scene. "There were a lot of ICE officers, three or four cars," Almarez told Reuters by phone. He said NYPD officers arrived about 10 minutes later. He said the man was only removed from his car after an ambulance arrived. At the shooting scene, where police strung yellow crime-scene tape to cordon off a city block, a woman standing on a balcony overlooking the area told officers they were "taking our children," according to a Reuters witness. headlines.article_text: Nasdaq CEO: Tokenization could unleash billions in trapped capital Skip Navigation Markets Business Investing Tech Politics & Policy Video Watchlist Investing Club PRO Livestream Menu Key Points Tokenization could allow banks and financial institutions to move collateral more efficiently, freeing up tens of billions of dollars in capital, Friedman said at TOKEN2049 in Singapore. The shift toward 24/7 trading would require major changes to financial infrastructure, with AI expected to play a growing role in real-time risk management. Kraken co-CEO Arjun Sethi said companies outside the U.S. are exploring tokenization and seeking greater access to American capital markets. In this article NDAQ Follow your favorite stocks CREATE FREE ACCOUNT Attendees at the Token2049 conference in Singapore, on Thursday, Oct. 8, 2026. The crypto conference runs through today. Photographer: Ore Huiying/Bloomberg via Getty Images Bloomberg | Bloomberg | Getty Images Tokenization could free up tens of billions of dollars in capital tied up in assets used as collateral across the global financial system, Nasdaq CEO Adena Friedman said. Tokenizing assets such as Treasurys, equities and money market funds, along with the flow of money, could make collateral more liquid, Friedman told CNBC's Joanna Ossinger at the TOKEN2049 conference in Singapore. "If you tokenize all those instruments along with the flow of money, then the collateral becomes very fluid," Friedman said. Tokenization involves representing financial assets, such as stocks and bonds, as digital tokens that can be transferred using blockchain technology. Friedman said institutional interest in tokenization has grown over the past year, pointing in part to the passage of the Genius Act in the U.S., which established a regulatory framework for stablecoins. "If we can tokenize money, then we can tokenize the flow of capital," she said. That growing institutional interest is converging with demand from retail investors, who have long sought the ability to trade around the clock, according to Friedman. The retail ecosystem "has been about 10 years ahead," she said. The push toward 24/7 trading Moving to a fully 24/7 market would be a major undertaking for the financial industry, Friedman said. "The easiest part is the exchange infrastructure," she said. Friedman said that financial institutions have traditionally had periods when markets are closed to update systems and manage risk. But operating around the clock would require those processes, including risk and collateral management, to take place continuously. "Everything has to be real time all the time," she said. Artificial intelligence could help financial institutions manage that transition. Nasdaq has launched a series of digital agents within its risk management platform that initially provide recommendations, Friedman said. Over time, banks could use those agents to take more direct action, she added. "AI is critical for 24/7," Friedman said. Bridging crypto and traditional finance Companies outside the U.S. are showing interest in tokenization and access to American capital markets, Arjun Sethi, co-CEO of cryptocurrency exchange Kraken, told CNBC. Sethi pointed to a company generating roughly $25 million in revenue that was exploring ways to access capital markets, as well as larger international companies interested in tokenization and U.S. public listings. He said tokenization could help expand access to capital markets for companies around the world. However, round-the-clock trading may not be suitable for everything, according to Friedman. "Not every asset is liquid enough to support a 24/7 environment," she said. Still, greater connectivity across the global financial system could also open up access to asset classes that were previously out of reach for some investors, Friedman said.
